title: Introduce tokenized-fingerprint probe reservoir with budgeted fallback guard
author: Maya Rodriguez
release_notes: Add tokenized-fingerprint probe reservoir to reduce noisy regression detections; introduce budgeted fallback policy to prevent canary storms; add dashboards and e2e tests.
description:
Summary: This PR implements a tokenized-fingerprint based probe reservoir and a budgeted fallback guard for the perf-canary service. Motivation: recent incidents showed cascaded canary rollbacks caused by correlated noisy probes (same token prefixes / traffic shards) and sudden probe storms during traffic ramps. The new reservoir hashes requests into tokenized fingerprints and enforces an entropy-anchored sampling policy so probe selection is both diverse and stable across short windows. A budgeted fallback prevents runaway probe traffic from triggering broad rollbacks during transients.

What changed (single continuous description): Added a new prober/reservoir implementation (pkg/prober/token_fingerprint_reservoir.go) and a lightweight resonance metric that tracks fingerprint reuse frequency. Implemented an entropy-anchored sampler in pkg/prober/sampler.go that biases selection to lower-reuse fingerprints while preserving representative traffic slices. Introduced a budgeted fallback guard in pkg/scheduler/budgeted_fallback.go which gates canary escalation when probe budget consumption exceeds adaptive thresholds. Updated canary orchestration to include the reservoir in the probe pipeline (pkg/orchestrator/probe_pipeline.go). Added a canary-sim harness (tools/canary-sim/sim_reservoir.py) used to verify behavior under synthetic traffic shapes and spike scenarios. Added e2e integration test (test/e2e/probe_reservoir_integration_test.go) and unit tests for sampler and budget logic (pkg/prober/*_test.go). Added dashboard and alert templates (charts/canary-dashboard/token-resonance.yaml) and metric names documented (docs/perf-canary/fingerprint-reservoir.md).

Commits (high-level):
- feat(reservoir): tokenized-fingerprint reservoir and reservoir API (Maya Rodriguez)
- feat(sampler): entropy-anchored sampler and sampling policy configs (Maya Rodriguez)
- feat(scheduler): budgeted fallback guard and gates (Maya Rodriguez)
- test: add simulation harness and e2e/integration tests (Maya Rodriguez)
- docs: usage, metrics, dashboard example (Maya Rodriguez)

Files touched (high-level list): pkg/prober/token_fingerprint_reservoir.go; pkg/prober/sampler.go; pkg/scheduler/budgeted_fallback.go; pkg/orchestrator/probe_pipeline.go; tools/canary-sim/sim_reservoir.py; test/e2e/probe_reservoir_integration_test.go; charts/canary-dashboard/token-resonance.yaml; docs/perf-canary/fingerprint-reservoir.md

Performance/behavior results from sim & canary run:
- Synthetic ramp test (1m to 100qps): reservoir reduced fingerprint reuse score variance by ~62% compared to current uniform sampler.
- Canary stability run (24h, mixed traffic): false-positive rollback triggers dropped from 4 to 1 in the test cohort.
- CPU overhead: sampler adds ~0.6% p99 request-side latency under probe-heavy workloads; throughput unaffected for normal request paths (negative path isolated to probe pipeline).

Checklist: [x] design doc link added to PR [x] unit tests added [x] e2e canary test added [x] dashboard + alerts [x] canary-sim reproducer included [x] feature-flag guarded (reservoir enabled by default for perf-canary envs)

Compatibility & rollout: The reservoir is feature-flagged and configurable by canary policy. Default policy is conservative (low probe concurrency + small reservoir window). Ops runbook updated in docs/perf-canary/runbooks/reservoir.md to describe quick disable and fallback thresholds.

Review conversation (condensed):
- Lena Park: "Nice approach to reduce correlated probe noise. Please add an explanation of the fingerprint hash collision risk and a quick amplification test."
- Maya Rodriguez: "Added a section in docs/perf-canary/fingerprint-reservoir.md (hash collision analysis) and included a collision test in tools/canary-sim/sim_reservoir.py."
- Daniel Ortega: "Requested change: expose resonance_score in the metrics with clear cardinality guidance so dashboards don't blow up."
- Maya Rodriguez: "Exposed resonance_score as a histogram (bucket config added) and added a sampler label to keep cardinality bounded. Updated charts token-resonance.yaml."
- Priya Menon: "CI flake noted in e2e when running with race detector; suggested test stabilization by using deterministic seed."
- Maya Rodriguez: "Stabilized tests with deterministic seed; pushed fix."
- CI: initial run had a lint error (unused import) which was fixed in second commit; all checks green on final run.

CI summary: unit tests passed, e2e passed in simulation and test cluster, linters and govet clean. One transient failure during first CI run (lint), fixed in follow-up commit; final status: pass.

Risk assessment & mitigations: The main risk is added complexity to probe selection which could under-sample rare but important traffic slices. Mitigations: conservative default sampling, canary policy limits, easy opt-out via feature flag, and additional monitoring (resonance_score, probe_coverage_rate).

Merge & follow-ups: Squash-merged to main on 2026-02-18 after approvals from reviewers. Follow-up tasks created: ENG-9187 (observe reservoir in production for two weeks), ENG-9234 (add automated revert playbook if cascade detected), and a small perf follow-up to micro-optimize fingerprint hashing for lower CPU overhead.

Notes for operators: To temporarily disable reservoir: set canary.policy.prober.reservoir.enabled=false in config or use the console rollout guard to switch probe routing to legacy sampler. Dashboard tile: canary/token_resonance (resonance_score p50/p95/p99).
